nodes.name: Quantum Brownian Motion channel
nodes.statement: The shared resource mode sent to Bob is affected by a decoherence process during its propagation; it is schematized by a non-Markovian Quantum Brownian Motion (QBM) channel~\cite{PhysRevD.45.2843, PhysRevA.67.042108, PhysRevA.70.032113}, described by the following master equation with time-dependent coefficients: \begin{align} \frac{d\rho}{dt} = & -\frac{i}{\hbar} [H_0,\rho(t)]-\Delta(t)[\hat{x},[\hat{x},\rho(t)]] + \nonumber \\ & + \Pi(t)[\hat{x},[\hat{p},\rho(t)]] - i\gamma(t)[\hat{x},\{\hat{p},\rho(t)\}]\;, \end{align} where $H_0$ is the fee hamiltonian of the system, the coefficient $\gamma(t)$ represent the damping factor, $\Delta(t)$ and $\Pi(t)$ are the normal diffusion and the anomalous diffusion coefficients respectively, and $\hat{x}$ and $\hat{p}$ are the quadrature operators.
nodes.origin_citation: Hu, Paz & Zhang 1992; Intravaia et al. 2003; Maniscalco et al. 2004
differentia: described by the following master equation with time-dependent coefficients
nodes.statement_short: The QBM channel: master equation with time-dependent damping $\gamma$, normal diffusion $\Delta$ and anomalous diffusion $\Pi$.
also_stated_at: Under these conditions the system evolution is described by the following master equation: \begin{align} \frac{d\rho}{dt} = & -\frac{i}{\hbar} [H_0,\rho(t)]-\Delta(t)[\hat{x},[\hat{x},\rho(t)]]+ \Pi(t)[\hat{x},[\hat{p},\rho(t)]] \nonumber \\ & -i\gamma(t)[\hat{x},\{\hat{p},\rho(t)\}]\;, \end{align} where $\Delta(t)$ and $\Pi(t)$ are, respectively, the normal and anomalous diffusion coefficients, $\gamma(t)$ is the damping coefficient, and $\hat{x}$ and $\hat{p}$ are the quadrature operators.

nodes.name: Ohmic-like spectral density
nodes.statement: In the following, we will consider the rather typical Ohmic-like spectral density $J(\omega)=\omega e^{-\omega/\omega_c}$, where $\omega_c$ is the cut-off frequency of the bath.

nodes.name: High-temperature regime
nodes.statement: In the high-temperature regime, namely the case in which the classical thermal energy is much larger than the typical one that characterizes the system evolution, one has $K_B T \gg \hbar \omega_c, \hbar \omega_0$, where $\omega_0$ is the characteristic frequency of the system.
also_stated_at: We work in the hight-temperature regime, namely the case in which the classical thermal energy scale is much larger than the typical ones that characterize the system evolution ($K_B T \gg \hbar \omega_c, \hbar \omega_0$).
nodes.statement_short: Assume the high-temperature regime $K_B T \gg \hbar\omega_c, \hbar\omega_0$.

nodes.name: Non-Markovianity parameter
nodes.statement: At any fixed given temperature and dimensionless time $\tau=\omega_c t$, the {\em non-Markovianity} parameter $x$ that characterizes the scales of the system time evolution identifies with the ratio between the bath and the system frequencies $x=\omega_c/\omega_0$: for $x\ll 1$, the dynamics is non-Markovian, otherwise it falls in the Markovian regime~\cite{PhysRevA.70.032113, TorreAsym2017}.
also_stated_at: in order to describe the evolution of the Bob mode in the QBM channel it is convenient to introduce the dimensionless time $\tau=\omega_c t$ and the non-Markovianity parameter $x=\omega_c/\omega_0$, where $\omega_0$ and $\omega_c$ are respectively the characteristic frequency of the system evolving in the channel and the characteristic frequency characterizing the time scale of the bath.
nodes.statement_short: Dimensionless time $\tau=\omega_c t$ and non-Markovianity parameter $x=\omega_c/\omega_0$; $x\ll1$ is the non-Markovian regime.

nodes.name: Two-mode squeezed vacuum resource
nodes.statement: The shared Gaussian entangled resource is taken in the class of two-mode squeezed vacuum states $\rho_{12}=S_{12}(\zeta)\ket{00}_{12}\prescript{}{12}{\bra{00}}S_{12}(\zeta)$, where $S_{12}(\zeta)=e^{\zeta a_1^\dag a_2^\dag-\zeta^* a_1 a_2}$ is the two-mode squeezing operator, with $\Re(\zeta)=\cosh(r)$, $\Im(\zeta)=e^{\imath\phi}\cosh(r)$, and $r$ and $\phi$ are, respectively, the amplitude and the phase of the squeezing.
nodes.statement_short: Shared resource is a two-mode squeezed vacuum with squeezing amplitude $r$ and phase $\phi$.

nodes.name: Channel transit time
nodes.statement: This transit time is defined as the difference $\delta t=t_f-t_0$ between the instant $t_0$ when the resource mode starts to evolve in the channel, and the instant $t_f$ when it reaches Bob.
also_stated_at: Finally, let us introduce the channel transit or travel time $\delta t=t_f-t_0$, given by the time interval that the quantum system spends travelling in the QBM channel.

nodes.name: Dimensionless channel transit time
nodes.statement: In order to characterize the state evolution in the QBM channel entirely in terms of dimensionless quantities, we introduce the dimensionless channel transit time $\delta\tau=\omega_c \delta t$.
also_stated_at: The dimensionless channel transit time is then defined as $\delta\tau = \omega_c\delta t$.

nodes.name: Teleportation fidelity under non-Markovian QBM noise
nodes.statement: In terms of the parameters that characterize the states and the channel, the teleportation fidelity reads (details are reported in the Appendix below~\cite{SuppMat}): \begin{align} &\mathcal{F}(r,\phi,\delta\tau,x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{ -4\bar{W}_{12}^2(\delta\tau,x)+\dfrac{1}{4} e^{-2\Gamma(\delta\tau,x)} \Lambda_{11} \Lambda_{22} }} \, , \end{align} where \begin{align} &\Lambda_{jj}\!=\!\cosh 2r +e^{\Gamma(\delta\tau,x)}\!\!\left(\!\!2\!+\!4\bar{W}_{jj}(\delta\tau,x)\!+2\dfrac{\mathcal{R}^2}{\mathcal{T}^2}\!+\!\cosh 2r\!\!\right) \nonumber\\ & + \qquad\quad 2e^{\Gamma(\delta\tau,x)/2}\cos\left(\phi-\dfrac{\delta\tau}{x}\right)\sinh 2r , \quad j=1,2 \, . \end{align}
assumptions: In terms of the parameters that characterize the states and the channel
nodes.statement_short: Closed-form teleportation fidelity as a function of squeezing $r$, phase $\phi$, transit time $\delta\tau$ and non-Markovianity $x$.

nodes.name: Beam-splitter transmissivity and reflectivity
nodes.statement: In the above, $\mathcal{T}$ and $\mathcal{R}=\sqrt{1-\mathcal{T}^2}$ are, respectively, the transmissivity and the reflectivity of the beam splitters that model the losses of the realistic Bell measurement performed by Alice and include the effects of the noise affecting Alice's shared resource mode.

nodes.name: Transit-time dependence of the optimal squeezing phase
nodes.statement: From Eqs.~(\ref{TelepFid}) we note that, at variance with the Markovian case~\cite{PhysRevA.81.012333}, the phase of the squeezing, whose choice contributes to select the best achievable efficiency of the protocol, acquires an explicit dependance on the channel transit time $\delta\tau$.
nodes.statement_short: Unlike the Markovian case, the optimal squeezing phase depends explicitly on the transit time $\delta\tau$.

nodes.name: Phase-optimized fidelity
nodes.statement: Consequently, we introduce the phase-optimized fidelity: \begin{equation} \mathcal{F}_{\textrm{opt}}(r, \delta\tau, x)=\max_{\phi}\mathcal{F}(r,\phi, \delta\tau, x) \, . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Optimal squeezing phase
nodes.statement: Due to the positivity of the master equation coefficients $\bar{W}_{11}(\delta\tau, x)$ and $\bar{W}_{22}(\delta\tau, x)$~\cite{PhysRevA.80.062324}, one finds that at fixed $x$ and $\delta\tau$ the maximum in Eq.~(\ref{OptFid}) is achieved by \begin{equation} \phi_{\textrm{opt}}(x,\delta\tau)=\pi+\dfrac{\delta\tau}{x} \, . \end{equation}
assumptions: the positivity of the  master equation coefficients $\bar{W}_{11}(\delta\tau, x)$ and $\bar{W}_{22}(\delta\tau, x)$~\cite{PhysRevA.80.062324}
conclusions: the maximum in Eq.~(\ref{OptFid}) is achieved by
nodes.statement_short: The fidelity is maximized by the squeezing phase $\phi_{opt}=\pi+\delta\tau/x$.

nodes.name: Markovian optimal squeezing phase
nodes.statement: In the Markovian limit $x\gg 1$ we recover the known result~\cite{PhysRevLett.95.150503} that the optimal phase of the squeezing that maximizes the teleportation fidelity is $\phi_{\textrm{opt}} = \pi$, independent of the channel transit time.
conclusions: the optimal phase of the squeezing that maximizes the teleportation fidelity is $\phi_{\textrm{opt}} = \pi$, independent of the channel transit time

nodes.name: Phase selection as a preparatory step
nodes.statement: Therefore a further step has to be included in the preparatory stage of the protocol: the optimal phase $\phi_{\textrm{opt}}$ of the shared squeezed resource has to be selected in the laboratory according to the value of the transit time $\delta \tau$ of Bob's mode in the non-Markovian channel.
nodes.statement_short: The optimal phase must be set in the lab according to the transit time of Bob's mode.

nodes.name: Logarithmic negativity of the shared resource
nodes.statement: Indeed, if one of the shared resource modes is subject to a quantum non-Markovian noise, the entanglement of the shared resource acquires a nontrivial dependance on the channel transit time: \begin{equation} E_{\mathcal{N}}(\delta\tau)=\max\{0,-\log\tilde{\nu}_-(\delta\tau)\} \, , \end{equation} where $\tilde{\nu}_-(\delta\tau)$ is the smallest symplectic eigenvalues of the covariance matrix of the state evolved in the channel~\cite{1751-8121-40-28-S01}.
also_stated_at: In order to quantify the entanglement of the shared resource state we resort to the logarithmic negativity, Eq.~(5) in the main text~\cite{1751-8121-40-28-S01}: \begin{displaymath} E_{\mathcal{N}}(\delta\tau)=\max\{0,-\log\tilde{\nu}_-(\delta\tau)\} \, , \end{displaymath} where $\tilde{\nu}_-(\delta\tau)$ is the smallest symplectic eigenvalue of the covariance matrix.
nodes.statement_short: Logarithmic negativity $E_N=\max\{0,-\log\tilde\nu_-\}$ of the channel-evolved resource, now transit-time dependent.

nodes.name: Equivalence between entanglement and optimal teleportation fidelity
nodes.statement: In the ideal, noiseless CV teleportation protocol with shared Gaussian entangled resource the optimal teleportation fidelity, i.e. the one obtained maximizing over all local single-mode operations, is in one-to-one correspondence with the entanglement of the shared resource, as first proved in Ref.~\cite{PhysRevLett.95.150503}.
assumptions: In the ideal, noiseless CV teleportation protocol with shared Gaussian entangled resource
conclusions: the optimal teleportation fidelity, i.e. the one obtained maximizing over all local single-mode operations, is in one-to-one correspondence with the entanglement of the shared resource

nodes.name: Recovery of entanglement-fidelity correspondence
nodes.statement: We see that indeed, in the presence of a non-Markovian dynamics the one-to-one correspondence between the shared entanglement and the optimal fidelity of the ideal noiseless protocol is essentially recovered.
assumptions: in the presence of a non-Markovian dynamics
conclusions: the one-to-one correspondence between the shared entanglement and the optimal fidelity of the ideal noiseless protocol is essentially recovered

nodes.name: Non-Markovianity increases fidelity with a delay
nodes.statement: An increasing non-Markovianity of the channel corresponds to an increasing teleportation fidelity, with a time delay.
conclusions: An increasing  non-Markovianity of the channel corresponds to an increasing teleportation fidelity, with a time delay.

nodes.name: Origin of the time delay
nodes.statement: The time shift is due to the fact that the correlation time scale of the environment $\tau_E$ is equal or greater than the relaxation time scale of the system $\tau_S$, corresponding to the rate of change of the state of the system due to the system-environment interaction, quantified by $x=\omega_c / \omega_0 = \tau_S / \tau_E$.
nodes.statement_short: The delay arises because the bath correlation time $\tau_E$ is at least the system relaxation time $\tau_S$.

nodes.name: Robustness across spectral densities
nodes.statement: The results of the present investigation encompass a large spectrum of interaction models, since they hold essentially for the entire family of spectral densities $J(\omega)=\omega_c(\frac{\omega}{\omega_c})^se^{-\omega/\omega_c}$, which for $s=1$ include the Ohmic case~\cite{PhysRevA.79.052120}.
assumptions: for the entire family of spectral densities $J(\omega)=\omega_c(\frac{\omega}{\omega_c})^se^{-\omega/\omega_c}$
conclusions: The results of the present investigation encompass a large spectrum of interaction models

nodes.name: Numerical check for sub- and supra-Ohmic baths
nodes.statement: We have also considered the sub-Ohmic ($s=\frac{1}{2}$) and supra-Ohmic ($s=3$) cases, obtaining qualitatively very similar results.
nodes.statement_short: Numerical evidence: repeating the computation for $s=1/2$ and $s=3$ gives qualitatively similar results.

nodes.name: Oscillator coupled to harmonic bath
nodes.statement: We consider the dynamics of a quantum mechanical oscillator with characteristic frequency $\omega_0$ in contact with a bath of harmonic oscillators via a position-position coupling and a factorized initial state.
nodes.section: 1.1 Quantum Brownian Motion channel

nodes.name: Weak-coupling QBM coefficients
nodes.statement: In the weak coupling regime, the explicit expressions of the coefficients read: \begin{align} \gamma(t)&\!=\!\alpha^2\!\int_0^t \, ds\int_0^{+\infty} \, d\omega J (\omega) \sin (\text{$\omega $s}) \sin (\text{$\omega_{0} $s}), \\ \Delta(t)&\!=\!\alpha^2\!\int_0^t \,\!\! ds\int_0^{+\infty} \, \!\!\!\!\!\!\!\! d\omega J (\omega) (2N(\omega , T)+1) \cos (\text{$\omega $s}) \cos (\text{$\omega_{0} $s}), \\ \Pi(t)&\!=\!\alpha^2\!\int_0^t \,\!\! ds\int_0^{+\infty} \, \!\!\!\!\!\!\!\! d\omega J (\omega) (2N(\omega , T)+1) \cos (\text{$\omega $s}) \sin (\text{$\omega_{0} $s}), \end{align} where $\alpha \ll 1$ is the coupling constant, $N(\omega , T)=[\exp(\hbar \omega/K_B T)-1]^{-1}$ is the mean photon number, $J(\omega)$ is the spectral density of the bath, that models the system-environment coupling, and $\omega_c$ is the cut-off frequency of the bath.
nodes.section: 1.1 Quantum Brownian Motion channel
nodes.origin_citation: Hu, Paz & Zhang 1992; Maniscalco et al. 2004
nodes.statement_short: Weak-coupling integral expressions for the damping and normal/anomalous diffusion coefficients in terms of $J(\omega)$.

nodes.name: Characteristic function and symplectic matrix
nodes.statement: When considering continuous variable systems it is useful to represent the state $\rho$ in terms of the characteristic function $\chi(\rho)[\Lambda]=\textrm{Tr}[\rho D(\Lambda)]$, where $D(\Lambda)=\exp[i S^\intercal \Omega\Lambda]$ is the displacement operator, \begin{equation} \Omega=\left(\begin{array}{cc} 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \end{array} \right) \end{equation} is the symplectic matrix, $S=(\hat{x},\hat{p})^\intercal$ is the vector of quadrature operators, and $\Lambda=(x,p)^\intercal$ is the vector of coordinates.
nodes.section: 1.1 Quantum Brownian Motion channel
nodes.statement_short: Characteristic function $\chi=\mathrm{Tr}[\rho D(\Lambda)]$ with displacement operator and symplectic matrix $\Omega$.

nodes.name: Solution of the QBM master equation
nodes.statement: In the characteristic function description the solution of the master equation Eq.~(\ref{HPZEq}) is~\cite{PhysRevA.67.042108, PhysRevA.70.032113}: \begin{equation} \chi(\Lambda, t)=\chi(e^{-\frac{\Gamma(t)}{2}}R^{-1}(t)\Lambda, 0)e^{-\Lambda^\intercal \bar{W}(t)\Lambda}, \end{equation} where: \begin{align} &\bar{W}(t)\!=\![R^{-1}(t)]^\intercal\!\!\left[e^{-\Gamma(t)}\!\!\!\int_0^t \!\!ds e^{\Gamma(s)}R^\intercal(s) M(s) R(s)\right]\!\!R^{-1}(t), \\ & M(s)\!=\!\left(\begin{array}{cc} \Delta(s)& -\Pi(s)/2 \\ -\Pi(s)/2 & 0 \end{array} \right), \\ & \\ \nonumber & R(t)=\left(\begin{array}{cc} \cos(\omega_0 t)& \sin(\omega_0 t) \\ -\sin(\omega_0 t)& \cos(\omega_0 t) \end{array} \right) \end{align} and where we have defined \begin{equation} \Gamma(t)=2\int_0^t \gamma(s)ds \, . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1.1 Quantum Brownian Motion channel
nodes.origin_citation: Intravaia, Maniscalco & Messina 2003; Maniscalco et al. 2004
nodes.statement_short: The QBM channel acts on the characteristic function by damped rotation $e^{-\Gamma/2}R^{-1}$ plus Gaussian factor $e^{-\Lambda^T\bar W\Lambda}$.

nodes.name: Input and resource projectors
nodes.statement: Let us denote by $\rho_{\textrm{in}}=|\phi\rangle_{\textrm{in}}\;_{\textrm{in}}{\langle\phi|}$ and $\rho_{\textrm{res}}=|\psi\rangle_{12}\;_{12}{\langle\psi|}$ the projectors corresponding, respectively, to the single-mode input state and with the two-mode entangled resource.
nodes.section: 1.2 Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Initial global characteristic function
nodes.statement: The total initial state $\rho_{0}=\rho_{\textrm{in}} \otimes \rho_{\textrm{res}}$ corresponds to the following characteristic function: \begin{align} &\chi_{0}(x_{\textrm{in}},p_{\textrm{in}};x_{1},p_{1};x_{2},p_{2})= \nonumber \\ &\;\; =\textrm{Tr}[\rho_{0} \; D_{\textrm{in}}(x_{\textrm{in}},p_{\textrm{in}})\, D_{1}(x_{1},p_{1})\, D_{2}(x_{2},p_{2})] \nonumber \\ &\;\;\;\;= \chi_{\textrm{in}}(x_{\textrm{in}},p_{\textrm{in}})\; \chi_{\textrm{res}}(x_{1},p_{1};x_{2},p_{2}) \,, \end{align} where $D_{j}(x_{j},p_j)$ denotes the displacement operator for the mode $j$ ($j=\textrm{in},1,2$), $\chi_{\textrm{in}}(x_{\textrm{in}},p_{\textrm{in}})$ is the characteristic function of the input state, and $\chi_{\textrm{res}}(x_{1},p_{1};x_{2},p_{2})$ is the characteristic function of the entangled resource.
nodes.section: 1.2 Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise
nodes.statement_short: Initial state $\rho_0=\rho_{in}\otimes\rho_{res}$ has factorized characteristic function $\chi_{in}\chi_{res}$.

nodes.name: CV quantum teleportation protocol with QBM channel
nodes.statement: Referring to the schematic representation of Fig.(1) in the main text, the first step of the protocol consists in a non-ideal Bell measurement performed by Alice, that is, an homodyne measurements on the first quadrature of the mode $1$ and on the second quadrature of the mode $\textrm{in}$. After such non-ideal Bell measurement, the remaining mode $2$ is left in a mixed state (see Ref.~\cite{PhysRevA.81.012333} for details). The result is then communicated by Alice to Bob through a classical channel whose gain factor is $g$~\cite{PhysRevA.81.012333}. The mode $2$ of the resource is sent to Bob through the QBM channel Eq.~(\ref{HPZEq}), the state evolution being described by Eq.~(\ref{chiEvol}). After receiving the mode 2, Bob finally performs on it a displacement operation.
nodes.section: 1.2 Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise
nodes.statement_short: Braunstein-Kimble-Vaidman CV teleportation with a lossy Bell measurement, classical gain $g$, and Bob's mode sent through the QBM channel.

nodes.name: Non-ideal Bell measurement
nodes.statement: Referring to the schematic representation of Fig.(1) in the main text, the first step of the protocol consists in a non-ideal Bell measurement performed by Alice, that is, an homodyne measurements on the first quadrature of the mode $1$ and on the second quadrature of the mode $\textrm{in}$. After such non-ideal Bell measurement, the remaining mode $2$ is left in a mixed state (see Ref.~\cite{PhysRevA.81.012333} for details).
nodes.section: 1.2 Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise
nodes.statement_short: Alice performs homodyne measurements on mode 1 and the input mode, leaving mode 2 mixed.

nodes.name: Classical communication
nodes.statement: The result is then communicated by Alice to Bob through a classical channel whose gain factor is $g$~\cite{PhysRevA.81.012333}.
nodes.section: 1.2 Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Channel propagation of mode 2
nodes.statement: The mode $2$ of the resource is sent to Bob through the QBM channel Eq.~(\ref{HPZEq}), the state evolution being described by Eq.~(\ref{chiEvol}).
nodes.section: 1.2 Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise
nodes.statement_short: Mode 2 propagates to Bob through the QBM channel.

nodes.name: Bob's displacement
nodes.statement: After receiving the mode 2, Bob finally performs on it a displacement operation.
nodes.section: 1.2 Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Output characteristic function
nodes.statement: Following Ref.~\cite{PhysRevA.81.012333}, it is straightforward to compute the characteristic function associated with the output teleported state: \begin{widetext} \begin{align} \chi_{\textrm{out}}(x_{2},p_{2},\delta\tau) & = \chi_{\textrm{in}}(g \mathcal{T} x_{2}, g \mathcal{T} p_{2})\times\nonumber \\ & \chi_{\textrm{res}}\left( g \mathcal{T} x_{2},-g \mathcal{T} p_{2};e^{-\frac{\Gamma(\delta\tau)}{2}} \left[x_{2}\cos(\dfrac{\delta\tau}{x})-p_{2} \sin(\dfrac{\delta\tau}{x})\right],e^{-\frac{\Gamma(\delta\tau)}{2}} \left[x_{2}\sin(\dfrac{\delta\tau}{x})+p_{2}\cos(\dfrac{\delta\tau}{x})\right]\right) \times \nonumber \\ & \exp\left[-\left(\bar{W}_{11}(\delta\tau)+\frac{g^{2} \mathcal{R}^{2}}{2}\right)x_{2}^{2}- \left(\bar{W}_{22}(\delta\tau)+\frac{g^{2} \mathcal{R}^{2}}{2}\right)p_{2}^{2}-2 \bar{W}_{12}(\delta\tau)x_{2}p_{2}\right] \, , \end{align} \end{widetext} where $\bar{W}_{11}(\delta\tau)$, $\bar{W}_{22}(\delta\tau)$, and $\bar{W}_{21}(\delta\tau)=\bar{W}_{12}(\delta\tau)$ are the components of the $\bar{W}$ matrix Eq.~(\ref{WBAR}), $\mathcal{T}$ and $\mathcal{R}$, with $\mathcal{T}^2 = 1 - \mathcal{R}^2$, are, respectively, the transmissivity and the reflexivity coefficients, that account for the non-ideal Bell measurement performed by Alice~\cite{PhysRevA.81.012333}.
nodes.section: 1.2 Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise
conclusions: \chi_{\textrm{out}}(x_{2},p_{2},\delta\tau) & = \chi_{\textrm{in}}(g \mathcal{T} x_{2}, g \mathcal{T} p_{2})\times\nonumber \\ & \chi_{\textrm{res}}\left( g \mathcal{T} x_{2},-g \mathcal{T} p_{2};e^{-\frac{\Gamma(\delta\tau)}{2}} \left[x_{2}\cos(\dfrac{\delta\tau}{x})-p_{2} \sin(\dfrac{\delta\tau}{x})\right],e^{-\frac{\Gamma(\delta\tau)}{2}} \left[x_{2}\sin(\dfrac{\delta\tau}{x})+p_{2}\cos(\dfrac{\delta\tau}{x})\right]\right) \times \nonumber \\ & \exp\left[-\left(\bar{W}_{11}(\delta\tau)+\frac{g^{2} \mathcal{R}^{2}}{2}\right)x_{2}^{2}- \left(\bar{W}_{22}(\delta\tau)+\frac{g^{2} \mathcal{R}^{2}}{2}\right)p_{2}^{2}-2 \bar{W}_{12}(\delta\tau)x_{2}p_{2}\right] \, ,
nodes.statement_short: Characteristic function of the teleported output state under the QBM channel and non-ideal Bell measurement.

nodes.name: Ideal-protocol limit
nodes.statement: The characteristic function for the ideal protocol is recovered in the limits $\mathcal{R} \rightarrow 0$ $(\mathcal{T} \rightarrow 1)$, $g \rightarrow 1$ and $\delta\tau \rightarrow 0$ $(\Gamma(\delta\tau) \rightarrow 0)$~\cite{PhysRevA.76.022301,PhysRevA.81.012333}.
nodes.section: 1.2 Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Teleportation fidelity (characteristic-function form)
nodes.statement: From Eq.~(\ref{EQCHIFIN}), the teleportation fidelity in the characteristic function description takes the following expression~\cite{Marian2006}: \begin{equation} \mathcal{F}(\delta\tau) = \frac{1}{2\pi} \int dx_2 dp_2 \; \chi_{\textrm{in}}(x_2, p_2) \chi_{\textrm{out}}(-x_2, -p_2,\delta\tau) \, . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1.2 Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Input and resource covariance matrices
nodes.statement: Given the input coherent state $\rho_{\textrm{in}}=\ket{\beta}_{\textrm{in}}\prescript{}{\textrm{in}}{\bra{\beta}}$; the two-mode vacuum state $\rho_{12}=S_{12}(\zeta)\ket{00}_{12}\prescript{}{12}{\bra{00}}S_{12}(\zeta)$ that constitutes the shared entangled resource, where $S_{12}(\zeta)=e^{\zeta a_1^\dag a_2^\dag-\zeta^* a_1 a_2}$ is the two-mode squeezing operator, $\Re(\zeta)=\cosh(r)$, $\Im(\zeta)=e^{\imath\phi}\cosh(r)$, with $r$ and $\phi$ being, respectively, the amplitude and the phase of the squeezing; and the $2 \times 2$ identity matrix $\mathbb{1}_2$, the corresponding covariance matrices read~\cite{ferraroLib}: \begin{align} & \sigma_{\textrm{in}}=\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{1}_2 \, , \\ & \sigma_{\textrm{res}}(r,\phi)=\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\begin{array}{cc} A(r) & C(r,\phi) \\ C(r,\phi) & A(r) \end{array} \right) \, , \end{align} with: \begin{align} &A(r)=\cosh(2 r)\mathbb{1}_2 \, , \\ &C(r,\phi)=\sinh(2 r)\left( \begin{array}{cc} \cos (\phi ) & \sin (\phi ) \\ \sin (\phi ) & -\cos (\phi ) \\ \end{array} \right) \, . \end{align}
nodes.section: 1.2 Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise
nodes.statement_short: Covariance matrices of the coherent input and the two-mode squeezed resource, with blocks $A(r)$ and $C(r,\phi)$.

nodes.name: Output covariance matrix
nodes.statement: Finally, collecting Eq.~(\ref{chiEvol}) and Eq.~(\ref{EQCHIFIN}), and Eqs.~(\ref{covin})--(\ref{C0RPhi}), the covariance matrix of the output state reads: \begin{widetext} \begin{equation} \sigma_{\textrm{out}}(r,\phi,\delta\tau)\!\!=\!\!\left\lbrace \frac{1}{2} e^{-\Gamma(\delta\tau) }\!\! \left[e^{\Gamma(\delta\tau) } g^2 \left(\mathcal{T}^2 \cosh (2 r)\!+\!2 \mathcal{R}^2\!+\!\mathcal{T}^2\right)\!+\!2 e^{\frac{\Gamma(\delta\tau)}{2}} g \mathcal{T} \sinh (2 r) \cos\left(\phi\!-\!\frac{\tau}{x}\right)\!+\!\cosh (2 r)\right] \right\rbrace\mathbb{1}_2+2\bar{W}(\delta\tau) \, . \end{equation} \end{widetext}
nodes.section: 1.2 Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise
conclusions: \sigma_{\textrm{out}}(r,\phi,\delta\tau)\!\!=\!\!\left\lbrace \frac{1}{2} e^{-\Gamma(\delta\tau) }\!\! \left[e^{\Gamma(\delta\tau) } g^2 \left(\mathcal{T}^2 \cosh (2 r)\!+\!2 \mathcal{R}^2\!+\!\mathcal{T}^2\right)\!+\!2 e^{\frac{\Gamma(\delta\tau)}{2}} g \mathcal{T} \sinh (2 r) \cos\left(\phi\!-\!\frac{\tau}{x}\right)\!+\!\cosh (2 r)\right] \right\rbrace\mathbb{1}_2+2\bar{W}(\delta\tau) \, .
nodes.statement_short: Explicit covariance matrix of the teleported output state.

nodes.name: Gaussian teleportation fidelity
nodes.statement: Indeed, due to the Gaussian nature of the input and output states, Eq.~(\ref{Fidelitychi}) can be written as: \begin{equation} \mathcal{F}(r,\phi,\delta \tau)=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\det[\sigma_{\textrm{in}}+\sigma_{\textrm{out}}(r,\phi,\delta\tau)]}}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1.2 Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise
assumptions: due to the Gaussian nature of the input and output states
nodes.statement_short: For Gaussian states the fidelity reduces to $1/\sqrt{\det(\sigma_{in}+\sigma_{out})}$.

nodes.name: Derivation of the teleportation fidelity
nodes.statement: Replacing Eq.~(\ref{SingmaOut}) in Eq.~(\ref{GaussFid}) we finally obtain Eq.~(2) and Eq.~(3) of the main text.
nodes.section: 1.2 Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise
nodes.statement_short: Substitute the output covariance matrix into the Gaussian fidelity formula.

nodes.name: Two-mode characteristic function evolution
nodes.statement: Given the noisy dynamics Eq.~(\ref{chiEvol}), the evolution of the resource state, in the characteristic function description, is given by: \begin{equation} \chi(X,t)=\chi\left[(\mathbb{1}_2\oplus R^{-1}(t))X,0\right]e^{-X^\intercal(0_2\oplus\bar{W})X} \, , \end{equation} where $X=(x_1,p_1,x_2,p_2)^\intercal$ is the vector of coordinates and $0_2$ is the $2\times 2$ null matrix.
nodes.section: 1.3 Entanglement of the shared resource
nodes.statement_short: Only mode 2 of the resource undergoes the QBM evolution of its characteristic function.

nodes.name: Evolved resource covariance matrix
nodes.statement: Due to the Gaussian nature both of the state and the evolution, the dynamics Eq.~(\ref{TMChiEvol}) can be expressed as a transformation on the covariance matrix of the input state Eq.~(\ref{TMRES})~\cite{EisWolf(2007)}. One has: \begin{widetext} \begin{equation} \sigma_{\textrm{res}}(r,\phi,\delta\tau)\!\!=\!\!\left[\mathbb{1}_2\oplus e^{-\frac{\Gamma(\delta\tau)}{2}}R^{-1}(\delta\tau)\right]^\intercal\!\!\sigma_{\textrm{res}}(r,\phi)\left[\mathbb{1}_2\oplus e^{-\frac{\Gamma(\delta\tau)}{2}}R^{-1}(\delta\tau)\right]\!\!+\!\!2\left[0_2\oplus\bar{W}(\delta\tau)\right] \, , \end{equation} \end{widetext} where we have expressed all quantities in terms of the dimensionless channel transit time $\delta \tau$.
nodes.section: 1.3 Entanglement of the shared resource
assumptions: Due to the Gaussian nature both of the state and the evolution
nodes.statement_short: The channel acts on the resource covariance matrix by a damped rotation on mode 2 plus noise $2\bar W$.

nodes.name: Block form of evolved resource covariance matrix
nodes.statement: It is useful to rewrite Eq.~(\ref{SigmaResEvol}) as: \begin{equation} \sigma_{\textrm{res}}(r,\phi,\delta\tau)=\left(\begin{array}{cc} A(r) & C(r,\phi,\delta\tau) \\ C(r,\phi,\delta\tau) & D(r,\phi,\delta\tau) \end{array} \right) \, , \end{equation} where $A(r)$ is the matrix defined in Eq.~(\ref{A0R}), and: \begin{align} & C(r,\delta\tau)=e^{-\frac{\Gamma(\delta\tau)}{2}}C(r,\phi)R^{-1}(\delta\tau) \, ,\\ & \nonumber \\ & D(r,\delta\tau)=e^{-\Gamma(\delta\tau)}A(r)-2\bar{W}(\delta\tau) \, . \end{align}
nodes.section: 1.3 Entanglement of the shared resource
nodes.statement_short: Writes the evolved covariance matrix in blocks $A$, $C(r,\delta\tau)$, $D(r,\delta\tau)$.

nodes.name: Smallest symplectic eigenvalue of partial transpose
nodes.statement: Its expression in terms of the submatrices composing the covariance matrix Eq.~(\ref{SigEvolt}) is given by~\cite{1751-8121-40-28-S01}: \begin{widetext} \begin{equation} \tilde{\nu}_-(r,\phi,\delta\tau)=\sqrt{\!{\dfrac{1}{2}}\tilde{\Delta}(r,\phi,\delta\tau)-\dfrac{1}{2}\!\sqrt{\tilde{\Delta}(r,\phi,\delta\tau)^2 -4\det[\sigma(r,\phi,\delta\tau)^2]}} \, , \end{equation} \end{widetext} with: \begin{equation} \tilde{\Delta}(r,\phi,\delta\tau)\!=\!\det[A(r)]+\det[D(r,\phi,\delta\tau)]\!-\!2\det[C(r,\phi,\delta\tau)] \, . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1.3 Entanglement of the shared resource
nodes.statement_short: Closed formula for $\tilde\nu_-$ via the symplectic invariant $\tilde\Delta=\det A+\det D-2\det C$.

nodes.name: Gaussian channel matrices (X, Y)
nodes.statement: The Gaussian nature of the QBM channel allows to characterize it in terms of two $2 \times 2 $ matrices $(X, Y)$, that act on the covariance matrix $\sigma$ of the input state as follows: \begin{displaymath} \sigma(t) = X(t)\sigma(0)X(t)^\intercal+Y(t) \, . \end{displaymath}
nodes.section: 1.4 Non-Markovianity measure of the QBM channel

nodes.name: Complete positivity condition for Gaussian channels
nodes.statement: For a Gaussian channel, the condition of Complete positivity (CP) is then expressed as: \begin{equation} Y(t)-\dfrac{\imath}{2}\Omega+\frac{\imath}{2}X(t)\Omega X(t)^\intercal \geq 0 \, , \end{equation} where $\Omega$ is the symplectic matrix defined in Eq.~(\ref{SympMat}).
nodes.section: 1.4 Non-Markovianity measure of the QBM channel

nodes.name: CP-divisibility violation criterion
nodes.statement: In Ref.~\cite{PhysRevLett.115.070401} we have shown that in any interval $[t, t+\epsilon]$, violation of the CP condition occurs if and only if \begin{equation} Y(t+\epsilon, t)-\dfrac{\imath}{2}\Omega+\frac{\imath}{2}X(t+\epsilon, t)\Omega X(t+\epsilon, t)^\intercal < 0 \, , \end{equation} where the matrices $(X(t+\epsilon, t), Y(t+\epsilon, t))$ are given by the following relations: \begin{align} & X(t+\epsilon, t)=X^{-1}(t+\epsilon, 0)X(t,0) \, , \nonumber \\ & Y(t+\epsilon, t)=Y(t+\epsilon, 0)-X(t+\epsilon, t)Y(t,0)X^\intercal(t+\epsilon, t) \, . \end{align}
nodes.section: 1.4 Non-Markovianity measure of the QBM channel
conclusions: violation of the CP condition occurs if and only if
equivalent_conditions: violation of the CP condition occurs
nodes.statement_short: The intermediate map on $[t,t+\epsilon]$ is not CP iff the matrix $Y-\tfrac{i}{2}\Omega+\tfrac{i}{2}X\Omega X^T$ is negative.

nodes.name: Punctual non-Markovianity measure
nodes.statement: A natural measure of punctual non-Markovianity, namely the non-Markovianity at any given time $t$, can then be defined in terms of the negative part of the spectrum of the matrix appearing in the l.h.s. of Ineq.~(\ref{CPINtMapViol}) as follows~\cite{PhysRevLett.115.070401,TorreAsym2017}: \begin{equation} \mathcal{N}_p(t)=\lim_{\epsilon\rightarrow 0^+}\dfrac{\sum_{i=1}^2\left(\vert\lambda_i(t+\epsilon, t)\vert-\lambda_i(t+\epsilon, t)\right)}{\sum_{i=1}^2\vert\lambda_i(t+\epsilon, t)\vert} \, , \end{equation} where $\lambda_i(t+\epsilon, t)$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix on the r.h.s. of Ineq.~(\ref{CPINtMapViol}).
nodes.section: 1.4 Non-Markovianity measure of the QBM channel
also_stated_at: Here we will employ the punctual measure of non-Markovianity $\mathcal{N}_p$ introduced in Ref.~\cite{PhysRevLett.115.070401} and defined in terms of a necessary and sufficient criterion based on the violation of the divisibility of the intermediate quantum dynamical maps~\cite{PhysRevLett.115.070401} (See the Appendix below~\cite{SuppMat} for details on the derivation of $\mathcal{N}_p$ and its properties).
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{N}_p(t)$: normalized weight of the negative eigenvalues of the intermediate-map CP matrix as $\epsilon\to0^+$.
